title: Staying United Against the Terrorism Threat
what_it_is: Staying United Against the Terrorism Threat

sections.label: Multiracialism against terrorism threat
sections.summary: Multiracialism is the foundation to defeat terrorism, and uniformed teams work together, but terrorism is not theirs alone to fight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Multiracialism is the bedrock, the foundation that will neutralise and defeat the ills terrorism seeks to sow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have effective, professional and responsive uniformed teams working to keep us safe − the Singapore Police Force (SPF), the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), working together with SAF, working in turn with the Internal Security Department (ISD) and the Security and Intelligence Division (SID).

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But terrorism is not a fight they are to battle against alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are three reasons: first, we face a regional threat; second, we face a global threat; and third, we have been specifically targeted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Misguided, they form terror cells which seek to influence others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: It is estimated that in the next two years, about 200 terrorists would be released from prisons in the region.

sections.label: Foiled Batam rocket attack plan
sections.summary: In 2016, plans to attack Singapore were foiled; terrorists from Batam planned a rocket attack on Marina Bay Sands in August 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In 2016, plans to attack Singapore were avoided and foiled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Terrorists from Batam planned to launch a rocket attack on Marina Bay Sands in August 2016.

sections.label: Three reasons for vigilance resilience
sections.summary: Because the region faces a heightened threat, the threat is global, and Singapore is explicitly targeted, vigilance and resilience must be promoted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: For these three reasons − one, our region is facing a heightened threat; two, the threat is global; and three, our country has been explicitly targeted − we need to promote vigilance and resilience.

sections.label: Australia amended military deployment laws
sections.summary: Australia amended its laws this year to allow military deployment alongside police personnel after a terror incident has been declared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Very interestingly, Australia amended their laws this year to allow military deployment alongside police personnel after a terror incident has been declared.

sections.label: Radicalised Singaporeans arrested statistics
sections.summary: 18 radicalised Singaporeans were arrested in the past two years, compared to 11 in the preceding seven years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Allow me, Sir, to move on to the second point, that we need to prevent the spread of radicalised teachings which promote violent extremism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: There were 18 radicalised Singaporeans arrested in the past two years, compared to 11 in the preceding years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Let us study that statistics: 18 in the past two years, compared to 11 in the preceding seven years.

sections.label: London Bridge Borough Market attack
sections.summary: The ringleader led a rampage that killed eight people and injured 48 others at London Bridge in Borough Market on 3 June this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In the end, that ringleader led a rampage which killed eight people and injured 48 others in an attack at London Bridge in Borough Market on 3 June this year.

sections.label: Radicalisation time now shorter
sections.summary: K Shanmugam said radicalisation once assessed at about two years can now take one or two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Minister K Shanmugam said that before the Islamic State militant group came on the scene, authorities assessed it will take about two years for individuals to become radicalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: But now, some individuals may be radicalised in as little as one or two months.

sections.label: Public Order Act permit refusal
sections.summary: Under section 7, the Commissioner of Police may refuse a permit for assemblies or processions that may glorify terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: For example, under section 7 of the Public Order Act, the Commissioner of Police may refuse to grant a permit if he is of the view that the proposed assembly or procession may glorify the commission or preparation of acts of terrorism, whether in the past or future.

sections.label: Penal Code and Sedition Act offences
sections.summary: Section 267C of the Penal Code and the Sedition Act make certain acts offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Section 267C of the Penal Code makes it an offence to distribute or possess documents or communicate electronic records that incite violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The Sedition Act makes it an offence to commit an act which has a seditious tendency.

sections.label: ISA detainees released on restraining orders
sections.summary: ISA detainees can be released from preventive detention and put on restraining orders after rehabilitation progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: ISA detainees can be released from preventive detention and put on restraining orders after they are shown to have made progress in rehabilitation and no longer pose a security threat that requires preventive detention.

sections.label: Multiracialism against terrorism
sections.summary: Multiracialism is described as the best socio-weapon to defeat the ills terrorism seeks to sow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Multiracialism is the best socio-weapon to defeat the ills terrorism seeks to sow.

sections.label: Women's relay national record
sections.summary: At the 2007 SEA Games, four women became the first local women's team under 45 seconds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In the 2007 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, women's 4x100-metre relay, Wendy Enn, Shanti Pereira, Dipna Lim-Prasad and Nur Izyln Zaini became the first local women's team to go under 45 seconds, cutting the national record from 45.51 to 44.96 seconds.

sections.label: Singapore tolerance rankings
sections.summary: Gallup World Poll 2016 and 2015 Legatum Prosperity Index ranked Singapore top for tolerance of ethnic minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: According to the Gallup World Poll 2016, Singapore ranked top out of over 140 countries for tolerance of ethnic minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: According to the 2015 Legatum Prosperity Index, Singapore ranked the highest among 142 countries where people feel that their country is tolerant of ethnic minorities.

sections.label: France ghettos after attacks
sections.summary: After the Charlie Hebdo attacks, Prime Minister Manuel Valls identified 64 ghettos in major French cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In France, after the Charlie Hebdo attacks on 7 January 2015, it was reported that the then Prime Minister Manuel Valls identified 64 ghettos in major cities where significant portions of the population were being left behind economically, marginalised into ethnic enclaves.

sections.label: HDB Ethnic Integration Policy
sections.summary: The HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy ensures racial diversity in each block of HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: When it comes to housing, the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's), Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) programme ensures that there will be racial diversity in each block of HDB flats.

sections.label: Multiracialism against terrorism
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore lets terrorism divide it or deploys a united multiracial force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: These are our anti-terror frontline task force patrol officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: But in Singapore, it is that same strong multiracialism that will be used to defeat the ills terrorism seeks to sow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In the very face of the threat, we deploy a united multiracial force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: So, I ask this House, do we let terrorism divide us?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Or do we say no, not on our soil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: When an attack vests on our shores, will Singapore shut down in fear?

sections.label: Infrastructure Protection Bill passed
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Protection Bill passed yesterday shows the Government's resolve to strengthen security measures against terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new Infrastructure Protection Bill that we passed yesterday is testament to the Government's resolve in ensuring that we continue to strengthen our security measures and minimise risks and threats, in light of the recent spate of terrorist attacks.

sections.label: RRG and upstream prevention
sections.summary: The RRG, set up in 2003, rehabilitates detainees, but there is a need to prevent radicalisation upstream.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The work of addressing and mitigating the threat of terrorism, radicalisation and extremist ideologies have traditionally been done by the RRG, first set up in 2003.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While RRG has been instrumental in rehabilitating Jemaah Islamiah detainees and their families, as well as ISIS supporters more recently, the work of rehabilitation is correction after the fact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There is a need to work further upstream in preventing radicalisation at its core, before it can even evolve into extremist ideologies or acts of terrorism.

sections.label: Youth ambassadors and counsellors
sections.summary: Youth ambassadors and leaders refer at-risk youths to counsellors and the RRG, with IHLs needed for training and projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These youth ambassadors and leaders are in constant touch with other trained counsellors and members of the RRG to help refer other youths who may be at risk of being radicalised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There is a need to work closely with our institutions of higher learning (IHLs) in the training of such youth ambassadors and leaders, and in supporting their socially constructive projects, such as Roses of Peace or Youth Ambassadors of Peace, appointed by several of our Muslim organisations.

sections.label: Islamic College of Singapore
sections.summary: The Islamic College of Singapore under MUIS is welcomed, letting students study Islamic education locally instead of overseas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to welcome the establishment of the Islamic College of Singapore under the ambit of the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS).

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Around 1,000 of our students are currently studying in Islamic educational institutions overseas and, in the context of an increasingly uncertain global security situation, I believe that having an Islamic College in Singapore will open opportunities for our students to further their studies in Islamic education at the post-secondary level within our shores.

sections.label: Preventing Islamophobia and racial profiling
sections.summary: People must prevent Islamophobia, racial stereotypes and profiling of Malays and Muslims, and Muslims need not feel apologetic for terrorist groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For instance, we need to work together to prevent Islamophobia, racial stereotypes or racial profiling against the Malays, or religious suspicion against the Muslims, from ever influencing the way we deal with one another, just because of the atrocities committed by ISIS, Al-Qaeda or other terrorist groups who claim to act on the Islamic faith.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And we cannot allow Muslims to feel apologetic for what these terrorist groups, which proclaim to carry out their heinous acts in the name of Islam, have done.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a Muslim, I abhor their actions and I refuse to be associated with them, and I refuse to feel apologetic for all they have done, for they do not represent me or the faith that I believe in and uphold.

sections.label: States punishing entire ethnic groups
sections.summary: Some states use overwhelming force against an entire people for the acts of a few, as allegedly in Myanmar with Rohingya Muslims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In other cases, some communities have to face up to a state that uses overwhelming force to punish an entire people or ethnic group because of the acts of a disproportionately small number.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We are already seeing this scenario allegedly play out in Myanmar where more than half a million Rohingya Muslims have been forced to abandon their villages, fearing more violence against them by the state.

sections.label: Buddhist Federation supporting MUIS relief
sections.summary: The Singapore Buddhist Federation and Buddhist institutions strongly supported MUIS's call to raise funds for victims of the Rakhine tragedy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The tragedy in the Rakhine state in Myanmar is not without controversy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But as a Singaporean, I was deeply moved to read of the Singapore Buddhist Federation and all Buddhist institutions strongly supporting the call by MUIS to raise funds to provide relief to victims of the tragedy.

sections.label: ISIS-inspired self-radicalisation threat
sections.summary: ISIS has inspired extremists, and self-radicalised Singaporeans joining ISIS add a dangerous dimension that security agencies cannot fully prevent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The advent of ISIS has inspired a new generation of extremists who find no compulsion using armed violence in any form against anyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Catalysed by developments in the Middle East and the rapid advancement of mobile technology, in particular, the prospects of self-radicalised and outwardly unsuspicious Singaporeans joining the ISIS cause have infused a dangerous new dimension to terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Well-equipped and well-endowed security agencies have nothing substantive in their arsenal to prevent a determined, lone wolf attacker from going on a knifing rampage or hijacking a truck and mowing down innocent people waiting for a bus, for example.

sections.label: Defending Malay/Muslim community from vilification
sections.summary: All Singaporeans must defend the Malay/Muslim community from vilification after an ISIS atrocity, as turning on any community serves terrorists' aims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the event of an ISIS atrocity, all Singaporeans, regardless of race, language or religion, must stand up to defend and protect the Malay/Muslim community from vilification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To reiterate, to turn on any community, let alone the Malay/Muslim community, would be to blindly walk into the playbook of the terrorists who seek to divide Singaporeans and justify their cause.

sections.label: Race and religion in hiring
sections.summary: Race or religion should never be reasons not to hire or to discriminate against someone, though workplace matters can be more complicated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I do appreciate that things can get more complicated in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But race or religion should never be reasons not to hire or to discriminate against someone.

sections.label: Give-and-take for multiracialism
sections.summary: Everyone must practise give-and-take and learn about one another's faiths to strengthen multiracialism and prepare Singapore against a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To live in peace and harmony, it is imperative everyone practises some give-and-take and accept that for multiracialism to succeed and thrive, we must move forward with a live and let live attitude with respect to our racial and religious differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government should look at how the good work of the IRO can be further enhanced and communicated in newer ways to better reach out to the next generation of Singaporeans and represent the common grounds Singaporeans must cherish and protect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, for tolerance to flourish, we must take the initiative as Singaporeans to learn more about and increase our knowledge and understanding of one another's faiths and practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This process must come from the bottom up, from within each Singaporean, and it is just as important as any movement to prepare Singapore for a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In doing so, we will unwittingly but crucially facilitate a deeper and more respectful understanding of one another and, by extension, strengthen our social bonds and the quality of our multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such an outcome will not only serve to inoculate Singapore against the negative fallout of a terrorist attack, it will represent the sort of society we strive to be and determine the Singapore we wish to leave behind for our children and our children's children.

sections.label: Singapore most religiously diverse country
sections.summary: A 2014 Pew Research Center study found Singapore the most religiously diverse of 233 territories and countries studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to a Pew Research Center study released in 2014, Singapore is the most religiously diverse country in the world, compared to the 233 territories and countries studied.

sections.label: Places of worship in Punggol
sections.summary: By deliberate design through the EIP, Punggol's mosque, temple and church are located within 500 metres of one another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For instance, our towns are multiracial from the onset by deliberate design through our EIP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Recognising the need to have places of worship to serve their respective communities, the mosque, temple and church each set up their places of worship in Punggol, a new town.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: They are located within 500 metres of one another.

sections.label: Extremist ideologies via online platforms
sections.summary: Extremist ideologies carrying persuasive but dangerous messages are finding their way to Singapore's shores via online platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Extremist ideologies are also finding their way to our shores via online platforms, carrying persuasive but dangerous messages.

sections.label: Local religious organisations and volunteers
sections.summary: Local religious organisations are mostly IRCC members, RRG volunteers, and religious leaders who pushed for compulsory Asatizah Recognition Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our local religious organisations are mostly members of our IRCCs, volunteers who make up our RRG, and religious leaders who have pushed for the Asatizah Recognition Scheme to be made compulsory.

sections.label: Virginia racial conflict deaths
sections.summary: The racial conflict in Virginia in August this year resulted in three deaths and dozens injured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The racial conflict in Virginia in August this year resulted in three deaths and dozens injured.

sections.label: EIP allows mixed-race living
sections.summary: EIP allows residents of different races to live together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, EIP allows residents of different races to live together.

sections.label: Muslim leaders and RRG contributions
sections.summary: Local Muslim leaders urged compulsory asatizah accreditation, and the RRG has contributed to preventing extremism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, recently, leaders from the local Muslim community urged that the accreditation of asatizahs be made compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, the RRG has also made active contributions to preventing extremism.

sections.label: RRG and Asatizah Recognition Scheme
sections.summary: RRG implements educational and rehabilitative processes for those lured by radical beliefs, while ARS ensures religious guidance fits Singapore's context and prevents violent teachings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The establishment of RRG is a measure to implement educational and rehabilitative processes for individuals who are lured and influenced by radical beliefs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) is another effort to ensure that religious guidance being delivered is in line with our context of Singaporeans of different backgrounds living together and, at the same time, prevent any teachings that are based on violence and radical ideologies.

sections.label: Religious Knowledge in secondary schools
sections.summary: The speaker suggests inculcating religious values at a young age through the national education system by reintroducing Religious Knowledge in secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to suggest that efforts to inculcate religious values at a young age should be done through the national education system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This can be done by reintroducing the Religious Knowledge (RK) subject in secondary schools.

sections.label: Countering mind manipulation via psychology
sections.summary: The speaker says minds are manipulated by planting perspectives that accept propaganda, and that learning Psychology can counter such manipulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The manipulation of minds is done by planting perspectives and perceptions that are prone to accept and allow such propaganda that is presented to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I feel that such manipulations can be countered by learning Psychology.

sections.label: Applauded move for social cohesion
sections.summary: The move was applauded and beneficial because the combination can produce individuals proud of their Singaporean identity, enhancing social cohesion efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This move has been applauded and has been very beneficial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because this combination can produce individuals who possess positive characteristics who are proud of their identity as Singaporeans, and this will further enhance efforts to strengthen social cohesion in Singapore.

sections.label: Multicultural success and terrorism threat
sections.summary: Because Singapore is a successful multicultural society, it is on the terrorist hit list, and terrorism threatens its hard-earned social fabric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Ironically, because we are a successful example of a multicultural society, we are on the terrorist hit list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Terrorism threatens to rip our hard-earned social fabric apart.

sections.label: Unattended bags ignored and unreported
sections.summary: Videos and posts online continue to show that unattended bags or items in public spaces were often ignored and unreported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, videos and posts online continue to show that unattended bags or items in public spaces were often ignored and unreported.

sections.label: EU calls for hate speech crackdown
sections.summary: The EU wants tech giants like Facebook and Twitter to do more against online hate speech, and the speaker asks whether Singapore will seek the same provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With regard to hate speech online, the European Union (EU) has said that it wants tech giants like Facebook and Twitter to do more in cracking down on hate speeches online by providing automatic deletion technology and other ways to prevent hate speech from being propagated online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could we also look into whether we will call for the same provisions from such companies?

sections.label: Terrorism attacks and need for resilience
sections.summary: Terrorism is often heard of, and incidents including recent London attacks remind everyone of the need to be vigilant and resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we often hear the word, "terrorism", both offline and online.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are a number of incidences, including the recent attacks in London, reminding everyone that there is a need not only to be vigilant but also a pertinent need to be resilient.

sections.label: Migrant workers in healthcare
sections.summary: The healthcare industry is supplemented by migrant workers from the Philippines, Myanmar, China, India and other countries, besides the Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the case of the healthcare industry, other than the Singaporean Core, the industry is supplemented by migrant workers from the Philippines, Myanmar, China, India and many other countries.

sections.label: Community Integration Fund support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Community Integration Fund launched by the National Integration Council in September 2009 and urges more organisations to tap it.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, I fully support the launch of the Community Integration Fund by the National Integration Council in September 2009 to support organisations in implementing ground-up integration initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge that more organisations should step forward to tap on this fund, not only to lessen the financial burden of these events' costs but, essentially, with the altruistic objective of promoting inclusivity and social well-being amongst employees.

sections.label: Companies need contingency plans
sections.summary: Companies must be better prepared with contingency plans or business continuity plans in the event of being succumbed to terrorist acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Companies must be better prepared with contingency plans or business continuity plans in the event of being succumbed to terrorist acts.

sections.label: SG Secure drills and counselling
sections.summary: Companies should be urged to perform SG Secure drills or tabletop exercises yearly, and encouraged through tax rebates or incentives to set up mental wellness counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, regardless of multinational companies (MNCs) or small and medium enterprises (SMEs), companies should be urged to perform SG Secure drills or at least tabletop exercises minimally once a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, companies must be encouraged through tax rebates or incentives to set up mental wellness or mental health counselling sessions for employees who are undergoing stress, depression or psychological challenges.

sections.label: Workplace first-aid and AEDs
sections.summary: Workplaces must be better prepared to provide first-aid or first line rescue such as CPR and be equipped with AED devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, we must ensure that workplaces are better prepared to provide first-aid or first line rescue, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and be equipped with automated external defibrillator (AED) devices.

sections.label: Ministry to promote workplace integration
sections.summary: The relevant Ministry should continue promoting workplace integration and use of available funds for diversity management programmes and Diversity Ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, the relevant Ministry to continue to promote workplace integration and the use of the available funds for companies to establish a framework that includes sustainable diversity management programmes and promote the establishment of "Diversity Ambassadors" to ensure unity in diversity and to propagate the message of workplace integration and workplace harmony.

sections.label: MUIS Friday sermon on Quran
sections.summary: MUIS explained in the 29 September Friday sermon that Quran verses should not be tweaked for convenience or alternative agendas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the Friday sermon on 29 September at all mosques in Singapore, MUIS did the right thing by explaining that verses contained in the Quran should not be tweaked for convenience and for setting of an alternative agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is a very apt reminder under the present circumstances where a Singaporean, reported to have been recruited by ISIS, is misleading Muslims in Singapore and in the region with false statements to follow his path of terror.

sections.label: MUIS introduces ARS registration
sections.summary: MUIS introduced the ARS last year to keep Muslims informed and register religious teachers for proper qualifications and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Keeping Muslims informed and ensuring that their need for proper and religious knowledge is not compromised as well, MUIS introduced the ARS last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To this end, registering religious teachers to ensure proper qualifications and training, and within the context of our multiracial and multi-religious society, is a welcome move.

sections.label: Poll on terror attack readiness
sections.summary: A recent Sunday Times poll shows four in five Singaporeans are not prepared for a terror attack, with Total Defence covering five key areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, a recent Sunday Times poll shows that four in five Singaporeans are not prepared for the eventuality of a terror attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A good example of this is our concept of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It focuses on five key areas − military, civil, economic, social and psychological.

sections.label: Racism and religious chauvinism in Singapore
sections.summary: The concept needs practice, and casual racism and religious chauvinism still exist in Singapore, often hidden away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It sounds very nice, warm and fuzzy but, in reality, it is a concept that needs lots of practice to make perfect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have to admit that even in Singapore, casual and sometimes even overt racism is still an ugly fact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Religious chauvinism is also becoming part of our landscape, yet this is often hidden away in the relative safety of inner sanctums.

sections.label: Racism and chauvinism near hate speech
sections.summary: Casual racism and religious chauvinism are just one step shy of hate speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Casual racism and religious chauvinism are just one step shy of hate speech.

sections.label: Conviction, harmony and terror risk
sections.summary: Conviction should not come from denigrating others, and we must not pay lip service to harmony because terror can strike at any point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The strength of our own conviction should not come from the denigrating of another's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But we must not pay lip service to the harmony that we enjoy, our multiculturalism and multiracialism, because terror can strike at any point.

sections.label: Founding of self-help groups
sections.summary: Self-help groups MENDAKI, CDAC, SINDA and later the Eurasian Association were founded.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Self-help groups, namely, the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community (Yayasan MENDAKI), the Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC) and the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA), and later the Eurasian Association, were founded.

sections.label: Founding of IRCCs
sections.summary: The IRCCs were founded to build trust across communities and invest in social capital through dialogue and friendship.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The IRCCs were founded then as a significant innovation to build trust across communities, to invest in social capital development through dialogue and friendship, so as to be ready for any adverse event threatening our cohesion.

sections.label: Multiracialism as foundation
sections.summary: Multiracialism is the foundation and is not ripped up to build defensive walls.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Multiracialism is our foundation and we do not rip up our foundation to build defensive walls.

sections.label: Collaborative self-help group initiatives
sections.summary: Collaborative tuition centres grew, MOE partnered with four self-help groups for 30 student care centres, and a pilot self-help group centre was set up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first is the growth in the number of collaborative tuition centres operated by the four self-help groups to help students of all races, which is an acceleration of the collaborative tuition programme started in 2002.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second is the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) strategic partnership with the four self-help groups to operate 30 student care centres for students of all races which was announced in August 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The third is the recent initiative by the four groups to set up the pilot self-help group centre in January next year to run race-neutral workshops and enrichment programmes to cater to everyone.

sections.label: Catalysing trans-racial collaborations
sections.summary: The Government could catalyse trans-racial collaborations by providing space, funds, administrative support, cohesion grants and public education synergies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this respect, I would like to suggest that the Government could help to catalyse these trans-racial, intercultural collaborations by providing three things: one, space, funds and administrative support; two, special cohesion grants; and three, synergies in the public education sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When I read about the self-help group centres in the news recently, I was thrilled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This initiative converges with the Workers' Party General Election (GE) 2015 manifesto proposal to set up multicultural help centres to house the race-based self-help groups, so as to provide mutual help and educational support to all underprivileged children in every town.

sections.label: Cohesion grants for learning trips
sections.summary: The Government could provide special cohesion grants to fund collaborative mutual learning trips and cultural studies research projects.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government could step in to provide special cohesion grants to fund collaborative mutual learning trips and cultural studies research projects involving collaboration between the universities and the social sector.

sections.label: Interculturalism as coming fourth phase
sections.summary: Interculturalism appears to be the coming fourth phase, and the Government would do well to facilitate its development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Interculturalism appears to be the coming fourth phase and the Government would do well to facilitate its development.

sections.label: Singapore's triple threat
sections.summary: Singapore faces a triple threat of extremist and radical ideology, segregationist beliefs and practices, and Islamophobia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: A few prominent religious leaders in the US have openly accused Islam of being a religion of violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So, Singapore is faced with a triple threat of extremist and radical ideology, segregationist beliefs and practices, and Islamophobia.

sections.label: Mandatory Asatizah Recognition Scheme
sections.summary: MUIS and PERGAS decided to make ARS mandatory, requiring asatizahs and IECPs to register before teaching Islam in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Last year, reflecting on the views and concerns raised by the community, MUIS and the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) decided to make ARS mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This meant that all existing and aspiring asatizahs and Islamic Education Centres and Providers (IECPs) must register with the Asatizah Recognition Board, headed by MUIS and PERGAS, before they can teach Islam in Singapore.

sections.label: Prohibited books and ARS numbers
sections.summary: His books were prohibited under the Undesirable Publications Act, and there are over 3,000 ARS-registered asatizahs and 174 IECPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In June this year, his books were prohibited under the Undesirable Publications Act, as they contained extremist views under the guise of "religious guidance".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To date, we have more than 3,000 ARS-registered asatizahs and Quranic teachers, as well as 174 IECPs.

sections.label: Programme and Singapore Islamic College
sections.summary: MUIS and NTU-RSIS developed a two-week programme, and MUIS has started looking into developing a Singapore Islamic College.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MUIS, together with the Nanyang Technological University (NTU)-S Rajaratnam School of International Studies (RSIS) Studies in Inter-Religious Relations in Plural Societies (SRP) has developed a two-week programme "Islamic Thought in Context: Living in Plural Societies" to familiarise returning graduates with the need to contextualise religious doctrines for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: While we have all these programmes in place, we want to do more to develop future religious teachers steeped in Islamic learning able to inculcate sound religious values that are appropriate for our unique Singapore context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So, I am glad that MUIS has started looking into the development of a Singapore Islamic College.

sections.label: Part-time programmes against extremism
sections.summary: MUIS has strengthened its part-time religious programmes to include lessons that inoculate youths against extremist influences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MUIS has strengthened its part-time religious programmes to include lessons that inoculate our youths against extremist influences.

sections.label: MUIS resilient families info-kit
sections.summary: MUIS developed and distributed an info-kit to help parents spot radicalisation signs and respond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MUIS has also developed and distributed an info-kit on "Resilient Families: Safeguarding Against Radicalism" to help parents identify tell-tale signs of a person who may be at risk of radicalisation and how parents can respond should such a situation arise.

sections.label: MUIS Asatizah Youth Network
sections.summary: MUIS is setting up an Asatizah Youth Network to complement the RRG's work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To complement the good work of RRG, MUIS is setting up an Asatizah Youth Network (AYN).

sections.label: New media anonymity and discord
sections.summary: New media and its anonymity have led individuals to denigrate religions or sow discord online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: New media and the anonymity it lends have led to individuals denigrating other religions or sowing discord among communities over the Internet, inadvertently or otherwise.

sections.label: ISIS influence and Islamophobia
sections.summary: Extremist influence spread by ISIS has resulted in Islamophobia pointing to Islam as propagating violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The extremist influence spread by ISIS has also resulted in Islamophobia which points to Islam as a religion that propagates violence.

sections.label: 9/11, JI and ISIS threats
sections.summary: Religious leaders and community stood together during 9/11 and JI, and ISIS now creates new threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: When we were tested with the 9/11 incident and the terrorist plot by JI in this region, including Singapore, our religious leaders and community stood together with the rest of Singapore to overcome those challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Now, the influence of ISIS has created new threats, especially through the manipulative use of social media to influence Muslims, and also to sow fear and suspicion in non-Muslims.

sections.label: ARS, Islamic College, parent outreach
sections.summary: ARS was made mandatory, MUIS is establishing an Islamic College, and has reached out to parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, ARS was made mandatory, and all asatizahs who wish to teach here must register themselves and abide by the ARS' Code of Ethics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Currently, MUIS is working hard to establish an Islamic College in Singapore in order to produce even more religious teachers who can support this objective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Apart from further improving the quality of part-time religious programmes, MUIS has reached out to parents so that they are more aware when they evaluate religious content and cyber addiction in their children.

sections.label: MUIS asatizah youth network
sections.summary: MUIS is forming a network of asatizahs and youth groups as first responders to young people seeking religious answers or at risk of dangerous ideologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To complement RRG's efforts, MUIS is forming a network of asatizahs and youth groups so that they will become the first line of response for young people who are seeking answers about religion and those at risk of being influenced by dangerous ideologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We must work together with the Government and all Singaporeans to defeat the triple threats of extremism, exclusivism and Islamophobia.

sections.label: Individuals fighting prejudice intolerance
sections.summary: More individuals should step forward, online or in the real world, to fight prejudice and intolerance towards one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: More individuals should step forward, whether online or in the real world, to fight prejudice and intolerance towards one another.

sections.label: Highest threat level vigilance
sections.summary: The current threat level is at the highest and security forces stay vigilant to prevent terror attacks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current threat level is at the highest and our security forces are staying vigilant all the time to prevent terror attacks from happening in Singapore.

sections.label: Preparing for eventual terror attack
sections.summary: It may not be a matter of if but when, so Singapore must be fully prepared for a terror attack eventually happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We may well already be in the situation whereby it is not a matter of "if", but "when".

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We must be fully prepared for the day when a terror attack eventually happens.

sections.label: Racial harmony after terror attack
sections.summary: The passage asks whether racial harmony can be maintained after a large-casualty terror attack, citing Government policies and institutions enshrining multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Should a terror attack in the pretext of race or religion happen and result in large casualties, can we continue to maintain racial harmony and not be mired in racial tensions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Since Independence, be it legislation, governance or policies, the Government has spent a lot of energy on formulating forward-looking policies to build a harmonious multiracial society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have integrated multiracialism as part of our country's core values and enshrined it into our pledge, the Constitution and the state institutions, such as the Presidential Council for Minority Rights (PCMR) and the Presidential Council for Religious Harmony (PCRH) under the President.

sections.label: Reserved Presidential Election system
sections.summary: The Reserved Presidential Election system was introduced to ensure that, every now and then, there will be a President from the minority groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Recently, we also introduced the Reserved Presidential Election system to make sure that, every now and then, there will be a President from the minority groups.

sections.label: Asatizah Accreditation Scheme under MUIS
sections.summary: The Asatizah Accreditation Scheme requires asatizahs to register with MUIS so their teachings suit Singapore's multi-religious society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, the Asatizah Accreditation Scheme under MUIS is very commendable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This scheme stipulates that asatizahs must register with MUIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is to make sure that their teachings can help the community practise their faith in a way that is suitable in our multi-religious society.

sections.label: Building multiracial society organically
sections.summary: It states the need to continue building Singapore's multiracial society organically and sustainably, with unity and resilience at critical times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Going forward, we need to continue to build our multiracial society in an organic and sustainable way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe this little red dot will be able to withstand the test by demonstrating our unity and resilience at critical times.

sections.label: Yusof Ishak on multiracialism
sections.summary: It quotes President Yusof bin Ishak's 1965 Address describing a tolerant multiracial, multilingual, multi-religious society and warning against extremism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The late President Yusof bin Ishak, in his first Address in this House in December 1965 upon Singapore's Independence, said as follows: "The four months since 9 August have given us time to take stock of our bearings, time in which to push emotions into the background for a calm and realistic appraisal of the new opportunities which Independence offers us, the greater authority to bring about what we have always thought necessary, a tolerant society, multiracial, multilingual, multi-religious, welded ever closer together by ties of common experience into a satisfying society, satisfying for both the indigenous peoples and those of migrant stock…Needless to say, the more extreme any community is about one race, one language and one religion, the more likely it is to arouse counter chauvinism amongst the other communities to the detriment of all." So, from the start, we see the implementation of multiracialism as a social weapon to ensure peace, prosperity and stability in our country.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew on groups left behind
sections.summary: It quotes Lee Kuan Yew's 1966 speech warning that groups left behind along racial lines would prevent a secure future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The late Mr Lee Kuan Yew recognised this when he stated in his first National Day Rally speech on 8 August 1966.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He said: "If groups are left behind either on the basis of language, race, religion or culture, and if for these groups the line of division coincides with the line of race, then we will not succeed in our long-term objective of a secure future." Hence, the importance of always ensuring social mobility and preventing a permanent underclass in appearing in our society, especially along racial lines.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community rehabilitation work
sections.summary: It notes the Malay/Muslim community's work to rehabilitate radicalised persons and prevent deviant teachings, acknowledging the RRG's work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the context of the recent incidents of Singaporeans being radicalised, we have seen our Malay/Muslim community working very hard to rehabilitate the persons involved and prevent the spread of deviant teachings leading to radicalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In particular, I wish to acknowledge the laudable work of the RRG to rehabilitate persons who have become radicalised through deviant teachings.

sections.label: Expanding group to other languages
sections.summary: It suggests there may be a case to expand the group to include people speaking Tamil, Malayalam and Bengali.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Given our experience of the language backgrounds of the persons arrested under the ISA in Singapore, there may be a case to expand the group to include people speaking in other languages, such as Tamil, Malayalam and Bengali.

sections.label: Far Right poll influence
sections.summary: Recent polls last month showed the Far Right receiving 13% of the popular vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Recent polls last month showed the Far Right getting more influence, receiving 13% of the popular vote.

sections.label: Survey on migrants and terrorism
sections.summary: Over 50% of those surveyed felt incoming migrants and refugees increased the likelihood of terrorism in their country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: More than 50% of people interviewed by the survey felt that the incoming migrants and refugees increased the likelihood of terrorism in their country.

sections.label: Hardening opinion against Muslims
sections.summary: In June 2017, the Minister for Home Affairs said internal surveys show opinion is hardening against Muslims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In June 2017, the hon Minister for Home Affairs mentioned that internal surveys show that opinion is hardening against Muslims.

sections.label: Bills, hate speech, social media
sections.summary: The speaker lauds recent Bills, suggests a German-style model for removing hate speech, and urges clarifying obligations while avoiding reactionary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My learned friend Mr Christopher de Souza outlined these pieces of legislation earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I laud the introduction of a good number of Bills in Parliament to further ready ourselves, the latest being the Infrastructure Protection Bill 2017 that was passed yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We may want to come to a consensus now on how to deal with any remaining issues, for example, as Mr Desmond Choo said, curbing hate speech and teachings via social media.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The passing of the German Network Enforcement Act in June 2017 will enable the authorities to require social media companies to remove hate speech from their platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we could consider a similar model in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the context of spousal communications privilege as provided for in the Evidence Act, or the right against self-incrimination if the disclosure will also expose the reporter to criminal liability, it would be good to delineate the responsibilities, clarify the obligations, so that everybody knows what is expected of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should avoid a reactionary approach like what happened in the US and UK after the 9/11 incident where pieces of legislation were passed with little scrutiny and debate.

sections.label: Brick and house foundation
sections.summary: Removing any one brick will weaken the house's foundation and it stands to be destroyed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Take out any one brick, the house's foundation will weaken and stand to be destroyed.

sections.label: Hiring despite colleague's warning
sections.summary: The speaker hired a person of a race a colleague warned about, and the employee was outstanding and promoted twice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Once, early on in my career, I wanted to hire someone of a particular race and a colleague told me that they had had bad experiences with employees of that race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I went ahead to hire this person anyway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That employee turned out to be outstanding and got promoted twice.

sections.label: Inter-ethnic marriages and complacency
sections.summary: The passage says rising inter-ethnic marriages may be a sign of progress but should not make us complacent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The rising number of inter-ethnic marriages may be a sign of progress − may be − but that should not make us complacent.

sections.label: Answer to a question
sections.summary: The speaker states that in their experience the answer to that question is a resounding yes today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my experience, the answer to that question is a resounding yes today.

sections.label: Middle ground on race speech
sections.summary: The passage proposes a middle ground of responsible, rule-bound public speech on race and warns against authoritarian solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Between the extremes of barring all public discussion of race except behind closed doors and the other extreme of allowing any kind of speech about race however irresponsible and hateful, there lies a middle ground − the middle ground of responsible, rule-bound public speech about issues of race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourthly, let us not use the very real danger of racial strife to reach for authoritarian, heavy-handed solutions at every turn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Yugoslavia under Tito, and Iraq under Saddam Hussein, there was little of the sectarian strife that broke out after those leaders were gone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But at what price was that peace achieved?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We can repress racial tension with the weapons of an authoritarian state.

sections.label: Hippocrates' first do no harm
sections.summary: The passage asks future Parliaments to remember Hippocrates' oath: first, do no harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, as we go forward into the future, as future Parliaments consider new policies towards multiracialism in decades to come, let us always remember the physician's oath set down by Hippocrates of ancient Greece − first, do no harm.

sections.label: Singapore multiracial policies and markets
sections.summary: The passage cites EIP, PCMR, GRCs and reserved Presidential elections as responses to failures in social and political markets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And that is why I am very glad that the Member speaking before also agrees that it is possible for social markets to fail, that we must never give in to the approach of free-market fundamentalism in social markets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is for similar reasons that in Singapore, we have our EIP, so that children of different races grow up as neighbours and friends from young.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is why we have the PCMR to scrutinise Parliament's legislation so that the majority does not discriminate against the minority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is why we have GRCs, to guarantee that minorities will always have representation in Parliament, guarding against failure in political markets, socio-political markets, so that every political party, as Mr Murali had said, if they want to mount a serious campaign nationally, they have to be multiracial and cannot play only to one race.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Recognising our human imperfections, we can understand why there is a hiatus-triggered reserved Presidential election, so that children from every race have a fair chance to see a President from their own community, at least once in a generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The earliest date another reserved election may be triggered would be in the year 2041.

sections.label: RRG established in 2003
sections.summary: The Government established the RRG in 2003 to rehabilitate self-radicalised individuals and understand self-radicalisation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government established the RRG in 2003 with the aim of rehabilitating self-radicalised individuals and to further understand the whole process or self-radicalisation.

sections.label: Free market, racial harmony, HDB estates
sections.summary: The free market may not create an ideal society, so EIP, PCMR and GRC uphold multiracialism, while some new HDB estates lack shared common spaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The so-called invisible hand of the free market may not necessarily be effective in creating an ideal society, particularly, in the aspects of racial harmony and social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is why we have the EIP, PCMR and the GRC system to uphold multiracialism in our society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In recent years, we see that many HDB estates do not have enough shared common spaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In some of the new HDB estates, the void decks are small and narrow, which will hamper the arrangement of community activities and also limit the opportunities for interaction among the neighbours, particularly, the young children.

sections.label: Racial harmony and counterterrorism responsibility
sections.summary: Racial harmony is not the responsibility of MCCY alone, and counterterrorism is not just MHA's responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As such, I must say that racial harmony is not the responsibility of MCCY alone, and counterterrorism is also not just the responsibility of MHA.

sections.label: Muslim distrust and radicalised Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker said non-Muslims should not distrust Muslims, and since then several Singaporeans were radicalised and detained over ISIS associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I added that non-Muslims should have no reason to distrust or be resentful of Muslims here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: That was a year ago, and we have since heard of several Singaporeans who were radicalised and have been detained because of their associations with ISIS as well as the one who had been featured in the ISIS propaganda video.

sections.label: Multiculturalism to counter distrust
sections.summary: The speaker supports investing in multiculturalism as a socio-weapon to counter distrust and the discord terrorism seeks to sow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to counter the distrust and I believe the way to do this is to build the relationships among the different communities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, fully support the call to invest in multiculturalism as a socio-weapon to counter the discord which terrorism seeks to sow.

sections.label: OnePeople.sg multicultural integration work
sections.summary: As a OnePeople.sg management committee member, the speaker sees hard work promoting multicultural integration; OPSG was founded by self-help groups, CDCs and PA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a member of the management committee of OnePeople.sg (OPSG), I also see the hard work put in to promote multicultural integration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: OPSG was founded by various self-help groups together with CDCs and PA.

sections.label: Muslims sharing accurate information about Islam
sections.summary: Non-Muslims who do not understand Islam may feel afraid, and Muslims in Singapore can share accurate information about Islam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Non-Muslims who may not understand this sacred religion will certainly feel afraid and do not believe the true teachings of Islam and its followers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think that Muslims in Singapore can play an important role in sharing and spreading accurate information about Islam.

sections.label: Johor Sultan rebuke incident
sections.summary: The incident drew a harsh rebuke from the Johor Sultan, who felt it was contrary to harmony and solidarity in that state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The incident resulted in a harsh rebuke from the Johor Sultan who felt that it was contrary to the principles of harmony and solidarity in that state.

sections.label: Islam logic and intellect
sections.summary: Islam is described as a religion based on logic and intellect that requires thinking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Islam is a religion based on logic and intellect; a religion that requires us to think.

sections.label: Religious knowledge and Singapore unity
sections.summary: The speaker urges Muslims to enhance knowledge, engage other religions and defeat terrorism, and supports the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Knowledge about what is permissible or forbidden is important, but what is more important is knowledge about moral values, ethics and the reasons behind any religious ritual that we perform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I truly hope that Muslims in Singapore will continue to enhance their knowledge, constantly try to engage people from other religions and work hand in hand to defeat terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, I wish to state my support for this Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have faith that if we stay true to our values as a multicultural, multi-religious Singapore and take effort to nurture our relationships with one another, we will be able to stay strong in the face of any challenges.

sections.label: National symbols and unity reminders
sections.summary: National anthem, pledge, National Day Parade, GRC, Reserved Presidential Election and EIP constantly remind Singaporeans of unity and multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From the national anthem played at the radio and TV stations, reciting the pledge in schools, the National Day Parade, GRC system, to the Reserved Presidential Election system and EIP, all these are constantly reminding Singaporeans the importance of unity and multiracialism.

sections.label: Bilingualism and common working language
sections.summary: Bilingualism lets Singaporeans share a common language while keeping mother tongues, and English aids equal communication and international dealings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Bilingualism enables Singaporeans to communicate with a common language while maintaining their mother tongue and helps develop multiculturalism in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Using English as the common working language will not only enable various races to communicate equally with a non-mother tongue language but also facilitate communication and business dealings with the international community and people from other countries.

sections.label: IRCC community scheme
sections.summary: The establishment of IRCCs is described as a very good community scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The establishment of IRCCs is a very good community scheme.

sections.label: Promoting understanding of other races
sections.summary: The speaker and grassroots believe understanding of other races' culture, faith and customs should continue to be promoted to strengthen trust and community bonds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From these incidences, my grassroots and I believe that we still need to continue to promote the understanding of the culture, faith and customs of other races through multiple channels, strengthen mutual trust and respect, and deepen our community bond.

sections.label: Building inclusive compassionate community
sections.summary: Singaporeans must work together to build an inclusive, compassionate community, being considerate and tolerant, and helping one another regardless of race, language or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): Singaporeans must continue to work together to build an inclusive and compassionate community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must be considerate and tolerant of the little differences which make our cultures so rich and unique, bearing in mind that we have more in common and share more similarities than differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We can only progress by helping one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The able caring for the less able, and those blessed with more must share with those who are less fortunate, regardless of race, language or religion.

sections.label: ISA detentions and radicalised foreign workers
sections.summary: ISA detentions have increased, and since 2015 over 40 foreign workers, including domestic helpers, were picked up for online ISIS radicalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The number detained under the ISA has increased, as Mr de Souza pointed out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Since 2015, we have also picked up over 40 foreign workers, domestic helpers included, who have been radicalised online by ISIS propaganda.

sections.label: SGSecure app devices
sections.summary: SGSecure was launched by the Prime Minister about a year ago, and there are now nearly one million devices with the SGSecure app.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SGSecure was launched by the Prime Minister about a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Today, we have nearly one million devices with the SGSecure app.

sections.label: Guides sent to workplaces

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: By early next year, 150,000 of these guides would be sent out to workplaces.

sections.label: Islamophobic attacks after London Bridge
sections.summary: London police collected data after this year's London Bridge attack and noted a fivefold increase in Islamophobic attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: London police collected data after the London Bridge attack this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They noted a fivefold increase in Islamophobic attacks.

sections.label: 2009 US race relations poll
sections.summary: An April 2009 New York Times/CBS News poll found 65% of Americans regarded race relations as generally good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In a New York Times/CBS News poll in April 2009, a few months after he took office, 65% of Americans regarded race relations as generally good.

sections.label: 2016 US race relations poll
sections.summary: The same poll in July 2016 found 69% of Americans saw race relations as generally bad and 26% as good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The same poll, done seven years later, July 2016, last year, 69% of Americans believed race relations were generally bad; with only 26% saying they were generally good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That was a 40% drop between 2009 and 2016.

sections.label: Activist multiracial harmony policy
sections.summary: The speaker rejects a laissez-faire approach to national identity and cites an activist policy fostering inter-religious and interracial harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have never believed that a laissez-faire approach in creating a national identity for a multiracial society will work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have had an activist policy of fostering inter-religious and interracial harmony.

sections.label: HDB shared community spaces
sections.summary: HDB safeguards gathering spaces in its designs, including precinct pavilions, three-generation playgrounds, roof-top gardens and community centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: HDB, when they design, they safeguard spaces where the communities can gather.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For new block designs, there are additional areas for interaction beyond the void deck, for example, precinct pavilions, three-generation playgrounds, roof-top gardens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There are dedicated spaces like community centres for people from different races to gather, bond.

sections.label: Pew religious diversity ranking
sections.summary: Ms Sun Xueling cited a Pew Research Centre study ranking Singapore top among 232 countries for religious diversity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ms Sun Xueling cited the Pew Research Centre study on religious diversity that Singapore is ranked top amongst 232 countries.

sections.label: 2017 country ranking comparison
sections.summary: In 2017 Singapore was ranked 151 out of 180 countries, below Guinea, Gambia, South Sudan, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2017, it ranked us 151 out of 180 countries, below countries like Guinea again; Gambia, where journalists were detained, media outlets shut down, Internet disconnected, international phone calls banned last year; South Sudan, where it was described as having one of the world's most serious refugee crisis, suffering the effects of a devastating civil war; Afghanistan is ranked ahead of us; Pakistan is ranked ahead of us.

sections.label: Non-Indian volunteer percentage
sections.summary: More non-Indian volunteers were obtained, but they were 11% while 89% remained Indian.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, we did get more non-Indian volunteers, but the percentage was 11%; 89% was still Indian.

sentences.text: Ten years ago, the four self-help groups came together with CDAC and they have OnePeople.sg.

sentences.text: The owner was asked to stop that discriminatory practice or shut down.

sections.label: Religious teachers and friendships
sections.summary: A problem exists if a religious teacher tells followers they cannot make friends with people of other faiths or an employer.
