sentences.text: Next, let me move on to religious teachers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There is also a problem if a religious teacher tells his followers that they cannot make friends with people of other faiths or an employer.

sections.label: Banning religious teacher's remarks
sections.summary: There was some unhappiness, but the approach of banning the religious teacher's remarks was taken without apologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There was some unhappiness, but I think Members will understand why.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said that "it is the biggest sin and crime for a Muslim to wish a non-Muslim Merry Christmas or Happy Deepavali", and I suppose the same goes for "Happy Chinese New Year".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And different segments of the community will drift apart.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we made no apologies for taking that approach, banning that.

sections.label: Glasgow Muslim shopkeeper stabbed
sections.summary: In 2016 a Muslim shopkeeper in Glasgow was stabbed to death by a fellow Muslim a day after posting a Happy Easter wish.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, in 2016, a Muslim shopkeeper in Glasgow was stabbed by a fellow Muslim to death a day after he put up a Facebook posting wishing customers "Happy Easter".

sections.label: Banned preachers including Mufti Menk
sections.summary: Mufti Menk was not the only preacher banned; two Christian preachers with Islamophobic comments were also banned weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mufti Menk, whom Members saw in the video, was not the only preacher I banned.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A few weeks ago, we banned two Christian preachers who had made several Islamophobic comments.

sections.label: Foreign preachers and hate speech
sections.summary: Foreign preachers not sharing religious harmony values will not be allowed to preach, and the process may be tightened.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Foreign preachers who do not share our values of religious harmony will not be allowed to preach in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But we have to try our best to insulate ourselves from overseas events and foreign doctrines which can do us serious harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are studying how we can tighten the process and ensure that such preachers do not come into Singapore to preach.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Desmond Choo said such comments have the potential to inflame emotions and can go viral.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are studying whether we need to move more quickly and have more options to deal with this particular issue appropriately and decisively when there is hate speech.

sections.label: Singapore Islamic College religious teachers
sections.summary: The Singapore Islamic College, when set up, can train religious teachers who understand Singapore's multi-religious and multiracial context.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Singapore Islamic College, when set up, can train a new generation of religious teachers who will understand our multi-religious and multiracial context.

sections.label: Reviewing Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act
sections.summary: Religion can strengthen society but exclusivist, intolerant practices deepen fault lines, so the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act is being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Religion can, and has been, a source of strength for our society, but we must also watch out for exclusivist, intolerant practices because that can deepen our fault lines and weaken our entire society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we are reviewing the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act to see how we can best deal with this issue.

sections.label: Terrorism and religious harmony caution
sections.summary: One must be careful about linking an entire religion to terrorism, which threatens Singapore's religiously diverse and harmonious society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Anyway, I would say that we have to be careful about linking an entire religion to terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Terrorism is not a threat that will go away anytime soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It threatens our very existence as one of the most religiously diverse and harmonious societies in the world, where different religious faiths have been able to co-exist peacefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We must resolve never to allow that and maintain the precious harmony that we have here.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As to the religious identity of that man, I based myself on what I read earlier in the morning but I stand corrected.

sections.label: Terrorist social media accounts
sections.summary: It states that while violent extremism may be propagated online, it can also be deterred, citing reported terrorist accounts and websites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: While it may propagate violent extremism, it can also be used to deter it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: It was reported by Channel NewsAsia that in 2015, there were 46,000 Twitter accounts and 10,000 accounts on Facebook held by those openly supporting terrorists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: There were another 9,800 websites belonging to terrorist groups.

sections.label: US collaboration and CBRNE detection
sections.summary: It states that collaboration with the US produced puffer portals for CBRNE threats and screening suites, and reports Shabu found in Marawi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Through collaboration with the US, we have developed puffer portals to detect all forms of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: We have utilised the Automated Biometric and Behavioural Screening Suite to identify many blacklisted travellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In Marawi, it was reported that 11 kilogrammes of high-grade methamphetamine hydrochloride or "Shabu" worth about US$5 million was found in a den belonging to militants.

sections.label: Faisal Manap on social cohesion
sections.summary: Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap suggested working upstream to intervene to strengthen social cohesion to fight terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap suggested working upstream to intervene to strengthen our social cohesion to fight terrorism.

sections.label: Ketupat making and workplace multiracialism
sections.summary: Dr Tan Wu Meng shared that Clementi CC held a ketupat-making demonstration for new citizens, and Ms Thanaletchimi highlighted the workplace for multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, speaking in all three languages, shared with us that the Clementi CC organised a demonstration of ketupat making for the new citizens to share with them Singapore's multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Ms Thanaletchimi highlighted the workplace as an important venue to foster multiracialism in Singapore.

sections.label: Daniel Goh on weapon wording
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked why the word "weapon" was used in the Motion's title.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked why the word "weapon" was used in the Motion's title.

sections.label: Community Emergency and Engagement Committee exercise
sections.summary: It states the Community Emergency and Engagement Committee is a platform for multiracialism, and describes a Ulu Pandan tabletop exercise simulating a terror attack response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The Community Emergency and Engagement Committee is another significant platform to ensure that our multiracialism can endure the test of a terror attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: This tabletop exercise was organised by Ulu Pandan constituency's Community Emergency and Engagement Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Our grassroots leaders and key community resource persons, such as religious group leaders, gathered to simulate responding to a terror attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Committee members were assigned to different groups, such as operations, media, logistics, community resources deployment, all everyday issues needed to overcome terror attacks.

sections.label: Choo Siu Heng Scholarship launch
sections.summary: In 2012 the Prime Minister launched the Choo Siu Heng Scholarship in Ulu Pandan, honouring a community leader and sponsoring a young Singaporean's university fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In 2012, the Prime Minister came to Ulu Pandan to launch the Choo Siu Heng Scholarship, named after a long-standing and selfless community leader who dedicated over 50 years of service to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Mr Choo was a source of great wisdom and encouragement, especially in how to reach out and serve residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: We decided to honour his legacy by setting up a scholarship in his name to sponsor the university fees of a young Singaporean who is involved in community work in Ulu Pandan.

sections.label: Singaporeans uniting against terrorism
sections.summary: The passage states trust that Singaporeans of all races will unite against terrorism and that Singapore will prevail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Instead, we trust that Singaporeans will lock hands with fellow Singaporeans of all races, face terrorism squarely, and show in unity that "we will not be defeated, not on these shores, not in our homes, not on our soil", and that Singapore will prevail.
